title: A compact mobile editor toolbar
highlights: On screens up to 540 px wide, the editor tools collapse into a hamburger menu with localized action labels and touch-friendly buttons.
The menu closes after choosing an action, pressing Escape or clicking outside. Larger screens retain the inline toolbar.
The standalone Yasgui bundle includes the updated editor. Unrelated packages retain their versions.
migration: No configuration changes are required. The responsive toolbar applies automatically when using the editor stylesheet.

title: Place complete results panels in host-owned layouts
highlights: Add optional resultsContainer and setResultsContainer() to the editor. Move renderer selection, status, loading, errors, documentation and downloads together while preserving live results and instance isolation.

The demo adds an icon button group beside the editor tools to switch between classic and query-left/results-right layouts. The active layout is indicated accessibly. These demo-only controls are hidden on screens up to 800px; narrow layouts stack the query and results.
migration:
Existing integrations keep their classic layout. To separate results, provide a same-document host outside the editor. The complete panel moves together, including renderer selection, status, loading, errors, documentation and downloads. Moving it preserves live results and pending execution.

```ts
const editor = createEditor(queryHost, {
  executor,
  renderers,
  resultsContainer: resultsHost,
});

editor.setResultsContainer(otherResultsHost); // Move the live panel.
editor.setResultsContainer(); // Restore the classic layout.
editor.destroy(); // Clean up owned DOM in both hosts.
```

Load the existing editor stylesheet and place shared CSS overrides on a common ancestor or both hosts. Language and themeMainColor changes apply to both sections. Destroy the editor before unmounting either host. The standalone Yasgui bundle includes the updated editor; unrelated packages retain their versions.

title: Sharing, consistent toolbar panels and prefix maintenance
highlights: Share queries from an inline panel: full editor links, automatically generated host-shortened links, SPARQL GET URLs, cURL POST/GET commands and a one-line query representation. Shortening is optional and provider-independent. Related: #11 and #14.
Short-link loading, retryable errors and stale-query protection keep the full link available. Explicit automatic-execution links require host opt-in; ordinary links remain non-executing.

Prefixes, sharing, keyboard shortcuts, settings and the plugin wizard now use consistent inline panels. Active toolbar icons highlight and toggle their panel; Escape restores focus. Format query is the first editor tool.
Add missing prefixes and remove unused prefixes from the prefix panel with one undoable edit. Analysis preserves literals, comments and used aliases; syntax errors prevent unsafe removal.

Clipboard-only copy buttons confirm success with a temporary checkmark and animation; screen readers receive a live announcement. Buttons share a consistent hover treatment and respect the theme and reduced-motion preferences.
The demo lets Cards grow to their content height, links all package names to npm, and adds project-wide release notes backed by Markdown in the repository.
The standalone Yasgui bundle includes the updated editor. Other packages keep their existing versions.

title: Editor resizing and smarter variable completion
highlights: Style table search and filter inputs inside the embedded editor without relying on demo form styles.

Add an accessible drag handle to resize the query editor, with keyboard controls and an option to hide it. Resizing switches to a fixed viewport and uses the existing row-count and auto-grow callbacks.
Complete variable names from the entire query, including variables used later in WHERE, while respecting subquery projections.

title: Full-height tables, map popups and keyboard help
highlights: Show tables at full height by default instead of inside a capped result panel. Add scroll: true and per-query table-scroll/table-height configuration, with Plugin wizard controls, to opt into a bounded viewport and large-result virtualization. Restore shared result-panel sizing when leaving the table. Update the renderer guide and packaged editor API documentation with defaults, validation, accessibility and performance considerations.
Add renderPopup for trusted host popup DOM in Leaflet and MapLibre maps. Hosts can provide lists and action buttons, or return undefined to retain the safe default popup.

Add an icon-only keyboard-shortcut overview in the right toolbar. The localized modal automatically shows Mac or Windows/Linux combinations, supports Escape and focus return, and can be hidden with controls.keyboardHelp. Document the new control and toolbar order.

Show the active platform's query-execution shortcut in Run tooltips (Command on Mac/iOS, Control on Windows/Linux), matching existing CodeMirror Mod bindings. Document keyboard shortcuts, focus scope, operating-system conflicts and host keymap extensions.
migration: Tables now expand to display all rows by default. To retain a bounded scroll viewport and large-result virtualization, configure `createTableRenderer({ scroll: true, viewportHeight: 480 })`, or add `# view=table; table-scroll=true; table-height=480` to the query header. The new map popup callback and keyboard-help controls are optional additions. See the [renderer guide](https://ldforge.nl/plugins.html#table) for details.

title: MIT licensing across LDForge
highlights: Change the LDForge license from EUPL-1.2 to MIT. Update package license metadata, bundled LICENSE files and license documentation. Third-party dependencies retain their own licenses.

title: Project information in the editor footer
highlights: A subtle info icon on the right of the editor footer opens project links with matching icons: documentation, GitHub, release notes and the MIT license. A miniature LDForge logo and title link to the project website, with an aligned copyright row at the bottom. The panel supports keyboard access, Escape and outside-click dismissal.
migration: The icon is enabled by default. Set `controls: { about: false }` to hide it; the icon remains available when query tabs are hidden.

title: Improved npm package discoverability
highlights: Add SPARQL, RDF, linked-data and semantic-web keywords to all eleven public LDForge packages, with additional keywords for each package’s editor, prefix catalog or result visualization capabilities.
